```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(here)

data_path  <- here("Data", "raw", "follow_up", "follow_up_data.csv")
output_dir <- here("Output", "follow_up")
fig_dir    <- here("Figures", "follow_up")
# Create directories if they don't exist
if(!dir.exists(params$output_dir)) dir.create(params$output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,

library(tidyverse)

```

# 1. Data Preparation and cleaning
```{r data-preparation}

# 1. Ensure output directories exist
if(!dir.exists(params$output_dir)) dir.create(params$output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# 2. Load the follow-up data using the defined parameter
followup_data <- read_csv(here(params$data_path))

# 3. Pivot data to long format for analysis
followup_data_long <- followup_data %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(ISI_FU:ISI_BSL, HADS_FU:HADS_BSL), 
    names_to = "variable", 
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>% 
  mutate(timepoint = case_when(
    str_detect(variable, "BSL") ~ "BSL",
    str_detect(variable, "FU") ~ "FU"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(variable = str_remove(variable, "_FU|_BSL"))

```

# 2.  Statistical Test Assumptions Testing
```{r assumptions-check}
# 1. Grubbs' Test for Outliers
grubbs_results <- followup_data_long %>%
  group_by(variable, timepoint) %>%
  summarise(
    grubbs_p = tryCatch(grubbs.test(value, type = 10)$p.value, error = function(e) NA),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Shapiro-Wilk Test (Using the "Split-Apply" method to avoid name clashes)
shapiro_results <- followup_data_long %>%
  # Create a combined key to split by
  mutate(group_key = paste(variable, timepoint, sep = "_")) %>%
  split(.$group_key) %>%
  map_df(~ {
    res <- shapiro.test(.x$value)
    data.frame(
      group = unique(.x$group_key),
      statistic = res$statistic,
      p_value = res$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
  # Separate the key back into clean columns
  separate(group, into = c("variable", "timepoint"), sep = "_")

# 3. Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variances
# We use the base-R 'leveneTest' logic within a tidy pipe to be safe
levene_results <- followup_data_long %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  levene_test(value ~ timepoint)

# Display results
knitr::kable(grubbs_results, caption = "Grubbs' Test for Outliers", digits = 3)
knitr::kable(shapiro_results, caption = "Shapiro-Wilk Normality Results", digits = 3)
knitr::kable(levene_results, caption = "Levene's Test for Homogeneity", digits = 3)
```


# 3. Combined Statistical Analysis: Manual Cohen's d and Change Scores
```{r statistical-analysis}
library(tidyverse)
library(flextable)
library(here)

# 1. Calculate the values exactly as they appear in your image
final_stats <- followup_data_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(change = FU - BSL) %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    bsl_mean_sd = paste0(round(mean(BSL, na.rm=T), 2), " (", round(sd(BSL, na.rm=T), 2), ")"),
    fu_mean_sd  = paste0(round(mean(FU, na.rm=T), 2), " (", round(sd(FU, na.rm=T), 2), ")"),
    mean_diff   = paste0(round(mean(change, na.rm=T), 2), "†"),
    ci_range    = paste0(round(mean(change, na.rm=T) - (qt(0.975, n-1) * (sd(change, na.rm=T)/sqrt(n))), 2), 
                         " to ", 
                         round(mean(change, na.rm=T) + (qt(0.975, n-1) * (sd(change, na.rm=T)/sqrt(n))), 2)),
    cohens_d    = round(mean(change, na.rm=T) / sd(change, na.rm=T), 2)
  ) %>%
  # Rename for the table headers
  select(
    "Characteristic" = variable,
    "Baseline\nN = 17" = bsl_mean_sd,
    "Week 4\nN = 17" = fu_mean_sd,
    "Mean Difference" = mean_diff,
    "95% CI" = ci_range,
    "Cohen's d" = cohens_d
  )

# 2. Create the Flextable
ft <- flextable(final_stats) %>%
  theme_booktabs() %>% # Professional academic lines
  autofit() %>%
  align(align = "center", part = "all") %>%
  align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all") %>%
  bold(part = "header")

# 3. Save to Word (This will NOT be empty!)
save_as_docx(ft, path = here(params$output_dir, "FollowUp_Results_Table.docx"))

# Preview in RStudio
ft
```

# 4. Data Visualisation
```{r visualisation, fig.width=8, fig.height=5"}

# Generate the plot
p_followup <- followup_data_long %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = timepoint, y = value, fill = timepoint)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "black") + 
  geom_line(aes(group = id), alpha = 0.4, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "fixed",
             labeller = labeller(variable = c("HADS" = "HADS-D"))) + 
  labs(x = "Timepoint", y = "Score") +
  # Use theme_classic for a clean start, then customize
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA, color = NA),
        # Ensure axis lines are solid black
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8),
        # Remove any remaining grid lines (just to be safe)
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("BSL" = "Baseline", "FU" = "Follow up")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("BSL" = "#a494d2", "FU" = "#62587d")) +
  expand_limits(y = 28)

# Print the plot
print(p_followup)

# Manually save a high-res version to your figures directory
# Manual save to Project Figures folder
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "follow_up_data.png"), p_followup, width = 7, height = 4.5)
```
